title: The Locked Gallery
overview: A respected curator is found dead after a private evening event at the Bellweather Museum. The gallery was locked, and the first account suggests an accident.
objective: Determine whether the death was accidental or deliberate, and identify the person whose access and account best fit the evidence.

hypotheses.statement: Deputy curator Elias Venn used a service key to enter the gallery and staged the death as an accident.
The curator suffered an accidental fall after the public event.

evidence.title: Initial incident report
evidence.content: The curator was found in the east gallery shortly after closing. No visitors remained in the building. The scene was secured for review.

evidence.title: Evening staff roster
evidence.content: Curator Mara Bell, deputy curator Elias Venn, guard Imani Cole, and conservator Peter Shaw worked the evening event.

evidence.title: Service corridor access log
evidence.content: A staff service key opened the east gallery door at 9:18 PM, after the public event ended. The key was assigned to Elias Venn.

evidence.title: Conservator's statement
evidence.content: Peter Shaw heard Elias ask Mara to meet privately in the east gallery. He later saw Elias leave alone and hurry toward the staff exit.

evidence.title: Scene review
evidence.content: The room layout and injury pattern are inconsistent with a simple fall. A small display stand had been moved and wiped clean.

suspects.name: Elias Venn
suspects.role: Deputy curator with a service key

witness_statements.statement: He heard Elias request a private meeting and saw him leave the gallery alone.

timeline.event: The public event ended and visitors left.
The east gallery was opened with Elias Venn's assigned service key.
Peter Shaw saw Elias leave the gallery alone.
